shared_elements: low-relief carving on a flat stone slab
glyph-like square/rounded blocks with internal detail
justification: Both surfaces carry low-relief carving composed of dense, rounded-square cartouches filled with small internal motifs, and B's ornament blocks (belt, headdress) share the same block-like glyphic convention seen throughout A, suggesting a comparable sign vocabulary. The decisive difference is that A depicts only a vertical double column of repeated glyph blocks with no figure, while B is dominated by a single frontal standing human figure in profile head with headdress, ornaments and flanking objects.
